findings.title: Limit scores use S(f=1) x f^2, which overstates the drawn shapes. The method text says the shape is measured, but it is not
findings.location: build-comparison/tools/compute_limits.js:62 (`score: round(S1 * f * f, 2)`), :72 (faceLow = S1 x 1.786^2), header comment :8; data/limits.json items/templates; data/settings.json limits.method; src/figure.js human() lines 145, 150-151 and 180
findings.evidence:
The comment at compute_limits.js:8 says "the score scales with f^2 because every width and depth scales by f". In Figure.human(), widthScale does not reach several parts: head (headB, headL, headH; line 150), hands and feet (line 151), the shoulder line (biacromial, line 145, which is also where the trapezius ends) and the leg axes (legAxis is fixed, line 180). Because the leg axes stay put, widened thighs overlap and the outline merges them at x=0.

I measured the figures the page draws for each limit (median-soldier template, stored f, arms at the stored rest angle) with the page's own Measure.measureSheet at 1,060 kg/m3 and 7.5% fat:
- arms, f=1.2539: 40.1 (page says 42.42)
- thighs, f=1.3464: 45.6 (page says 48.91)
- face, f=2.837: 191.7 (page says 217.14)

An analytic slice integral of the same drawn shapes gives f^2 / (V(f)/V(1)):
- median soldier: 1.070 (arms), 1.089 (thighs), 1.236 (face)
- across the six templates: 1.04-1.10 (arms, excluding Coleman), 1.04-1.12 (thighs), 1.16-1.27 (face)

With the tool and arms at 60 degrees, the face-limit shapes measure 158-196, where limits.json stores 181-233.

The page contradicts itself. Its own target tool, asked for 42.42 on the median-soldier base, replies "every width and depth × 1.28: it measures 42.0". The arms limit uses f=1.254.

Knock-on effects on the page:
- The arms headline (42.42) sits above HUMAN_TOP (41.50, Big Ramy's top), so gap 1 says "Two limits of the drawn body fall in this stretch: arms ... (about 42) and thighs ... (about 49)". Measured, the arms limit is about 40, below the human top.
- The face band top (233) reaches past Ollie's top (216.2), so "Empty to the end" says the face limit "lies somewhere from 86 to 230, across this stretch and beyond". Measured, the band tops out at about 196 and stays below 216.

Scripts: scratchpad/review1/limits_check2.js, limits_f2.js, parts.js, target.js.
findings.expected: Data/settings.json method says "that shape's score is read with the measuring tool at 1,060 kg/m³ and 7.5% fat". So the score at each limit should be the tool's reading of the widened figure itself: about 40 (arms), 46 (thighs) and 190 (face, contact geometry) for the median soldier. The same applies to the pessimistic face bound: measure the shape at f=1.786, not 26.98 x 1.786^2.
findings.fix: In compute_limits.js, replace S1*f*f with a measurement of the widened figure. Render make(f, Math.max(35, rest)).front and .side with Fig.renderSheet and measure with M.measureSheet({heightM: 1.8, heightRef: 'top', density: 1060, bodyFatPct: 7.5}), as app.html drawTarget does. Do the same for faceLow at f = pessimistic_girth_factor, then regenerate limits.json. If f^2 is kept instead, correct the comment and the method text: say the head, hands, feet and shoulder breadth are not widened and that f^2 overstates the drawn shape by about 4-12% (arms, thighs) and 16-27% (face).

findings.title: The page puts the arms and thighs limits in the empty stretch above every real man, but its own tests say its bodybuilder figures (score 39) are already past both
findings.location: src/app.html gapCopy ("limits of the drawn body fall in this stretch", about line 713) and figureOf (line ~739, Figure.human with default armDeg 20); data/limits.json templates.ronnie_coleman; data/settings.json limits.verdict
findings.evidence:
I ran the page's own limit tests (Figure.armRestAngle, Figure.thighContact) on the chart's own figures: Figure.human at each build's height and girths, as figureOf draws them.
- Ronnie Coleman: arms rest at 39.4°, thighs touch fraction 1.00
- Big Ramy: 39.7°, 1.00
- Eddie Hall: 35.1°, 0.82
- Kingpin: 34.9°, 0.84
- Hulk 77.8°, Abomination 84.1°, Juggernaut 73.8°, Thor 63.8° (all 1.00)
The arms limit is defined at 30° and the thighs limit at fraction 1. limits.json says the same: Coleman's template has arm_rest_angle_at_f1_deg 39.4 and reaches the thighs limit at f 0.9711 (<1).

The page says otherwise. Gap 'Score 42 to 62' reads: "From here on every score is an extrapolation: no real man on this chart scores above 42. ... Two limits of the drawn body fall in this stretch: arms can no longer hang down by the sides (about 42) and thighs touch all the way to the knee (about 49)." The limits verdict reads: "Widen the average soldier ... the arms are forced out first".

The chart draws every figure with arms at 20°. Coleman's and the giants' arms pass through their torsos (shots/390-details-coleman.png).

The band's low ends (36.51 arms, 42.38 thighs) come from Coleman's template scored by drawn volume: S(f=1) = 44.94. His chart score from his weight is 39.16, and the page's own drawing check says "that weighs 20% more than the weight counted". On the chart's footing his limits would be 36.51 x 39.16/44.94 = 31.8 (arms) and 36.9 (thighs).

Scripts: inline node runs of armRestAngle and thighContact (see the transcript); drawers3.js; gaptext.js.
findings.expected: By the page's own geometry, the top bodybuilders' outlines (about 39) already meet the arms and thighs tests, and the heavy strongman and Kingpin outlines (about 37-40) meet the arms test. The page should not imply that only bodies above 42-49 reach these limits.
findings.fix:
Three changes:
1. Say in the gap copy and the limit cards that the chart's top bodybuilders (Coleman, Big Ramy, about 39) already meet both tests, and Hall and Kingpin meet the arms test. Headline each limit by its band, or by the lowest chart build whose own figure meets it, not by the widened median soldier alone.
2. Draw chart figures at Math.max(20, armRestAngle) so arms do not pass through bodies.
3. Put template limits on the chart's footing by scaling each template's limits by its chart score / S(f=1), or score templates from their weight.

findings.title: The target-outline tool misses targets in its stated 15-900 range and hands over sheets the measuring tool rejects
findings.location: src/app.html drawTarget (about lines 1499-1530: f = sqrt(t/S1) plus one correction); tools/export_targets.js solve() line 46 (bisection only up to f = 6) and line 89 (one sqrt correction); src/figure.js deltoid cap (deltR scaled by f)
findings.evidence:
Page tool ("Draw an outline for any score", hint "15 to 900"):
- median-soldier base: 217 gives "it measures 202.8 (target 217)", 600 gives 579.5, 900 gives 762.4
- Coleman base: 217 gives 205.1, 600 gives 450.3, 900 gives 586.3

The measured score grows slower than f^2:
- median soldier: f=6 gives 596; f=7 gives 725 (rejected); f=8 gives 845 (rejected)
- Coleman: f=3 gives 256; f=4 gives 356 (rejected); f=8 gives 661 (rejected)
So 900 is out of reach for these bases with f up to 8, and sheets from Coleman f>=4 or median-soldier f>=7 fail the tool's own checks.

Cause of the rejections: the deltoid cap widens with f and rises above the skull. The front outline top is 1.943 m on a 1.80 m figure (Coleman, f=4) and 1.897 m (median soldier, f=7), so the views differ 5-8% in height.

node tools/export_targets.js --score 900 prints "widths x 7.348 ... measured score 770.6 (target 900); checks: FAIL view heights agree within 2%; ... FAIL side-view neck lines up ..." and writes the PNGs anyway. --score 600 --build ronnie_coleman gives 561.4 with the same FAILs.

The page's target status never shows the checks.

Scripts: target.js; inline measureTemplate sweep; export runs into scratchpad/review1/tgt.
findings.expected: BRIEF.md: "export the outline for any target score" for gap fillers, which are needed in 216-924. The tool should converge to the target, or say the target is out of reach for this base. It should not emit a control sheet its own checker rejects.
findings.fix:
Three changes:
1. In both places, solve to convergence by bisection or secant on the measured score with an expanding upper bound, not one sqrt correction.
2. Check r.ok; show failed checks in targetStatus and refuse to write or export a rejected sheet.
3. Keep the figure top at the skull: clip the deltoid cap below it, or measure with skull rows. State the highest score each base can reach, or limit the input to it.

findings.title: Wrong explanation: the 95th-percentile soldier scores lower because of his assumed body fat, not his height
findings.location: data/settings.json stops[0].sub ("under25" band): "The 95th scores lower than the median because he is taller, not more muscular."
findings.evidence:
model.evaluate gives:
- median (p50): S 21.04 at 25.3% fat; W/H^3 = 84.6/1.755^3 = 15.65
- 95th (p95): S 20.15 at 33.9% fat (official equation 32.4, Taylor 35.4); W/H^3 = 110.69/1.87^3 = 16.93, which is 8% higher than the median's
At the median's 25.3% fat, the 95th would score 1.8 x 110.69 x 0.747 / 1.87^3 = 22.76, above the median's 21.04.
findings.expected: S divides out height cubed. The 95th composite's lower score comes entirely from the 8.6-point higher body fat that the Army equations give his 113 cm waist.
findings.fix: Reword, for example: "The 95th scores lower than the median because the Army equations give him much more fat (34% against 25%); at the median's body fat he would score about 23."

findings.title: limits.json can go stale against settings.json, and the published page shipped a corrected note in its old form
findings.location: data/limits.json (generated by tools/compute_limits.js, "Do not edit by hand"); .github/workflows/test.yml (no regeneration or diff for limits.json); test/test.js (no limits.json sync test)
findings.evidence: At commit 3cd65f5 (first publish), running compute_limits.run() and comparing with data/limits.json differed only in `notes`. The page rendered the stale third note: "A softer line comes earlier: with the elbow held to 120°, people still manage eating, drinking and washing ...". settings.json already had the verifier-corrected text: "... 49 of 50 people still managed ..., the lowest setting tested." (I confirmed this by grepping dist/index.html.) The current working tree has since regenerated limits.json (uncommitted), but nothing in CI or the tests would catch a repeat. outline.json and duo-outlines.json each have a "file is what the tool derives" test; limits.json has none.
findings.expected: A generated data file the page reads should be checked against its generator, as CLAUDE.md requires for generated files.
findings.fix: Add a test to test/test.js asserting that JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(require('../tools/compute_limits.js').run())) deep-equals data/limits.json, as the existing outline.json and duo-outlines.json tests do. Alternatively, regenerate it in CI and git diff --exit-code.

findings.title: The limits test checks a function the arms limit does not use
findings.location: build-comparison/test/test.js:268-281 ('limits: wider at fixed bones, the thighs touch further down and the arms are pushed out')
findings.evidence: The test calls Fig.armBoneClearance(x) (line 274) and asserts armBoneClearance(base) === 0. compute_limits.js computes the arms limit with Fig.armRestAngle (rebuilding the figure at each angle), which gives 7.7° for the median soldier at f=1. No test touches armRestAngle, solveScale, elbowFlexion, the crease calibration, or the stored limit scores (42.42 / 48.91 / 217.14), so F1 passes the suite.
findings.expected: A test named for the arms limit should test the code that computes it, and the limit scores should be pinned to the drawn shape.
findings.fix: Test Fig.armRestAngle((deg) => mk(f, deg)) for monotonic growth and for reaching 30° near the stored f. Add a test that the stored limit score equals the measuring tool's reading of make(f) within a few percent, which would also catch F1.

findings.title: sliceRotated looks up a k profile by rotated-grid row, not by image row
findings.location: build-comparison/src/measure.js:471 (`vol += Math.PI / 4 * kf(r) * s * 0.5`) via frontOnly (part.kPoints together with part.angle)
findings.evidence:
Test case: a 40 x 100 px rectangle at rows 100-199 with k = kProfile([[100,1],[200,0.5]]).
- sliceRows: 94,562 px^3 (exact: 94,562)
- sliceRotated at angle 0.001°: 110,113 px^3 (+16%)
kf(r) receives the rotated-grid index r (0..2 x height), not the image row that kProfile expects. The current duo config gives no part both kPoints and an angle, so Rex's 2.545 m³ is unaffected, but frontOnly documents that combination as valid.
findings.expected: With a k profile, a tilted part's slices should use k at their image row, so that sliceRotated matches sliceRows as the angle goes to 0.
findings.fix: Track the image row of each rotated-grid row (for example, the mean original y of its samples, or y = u*cos(a) - v*sin(a) at the run centre) and pass that to kf. Alternatively, refuse kPoints together with angle in frontOnly.

verified_ok: Scores, ranges and plain FFMI recomputed with my own formulas for 22 builds across every group (Banner, ANSUR p5/p50/p95/largest arm, NHANES, Kouri, Reeves, Withers, Coleman, Big Ramy, Shaw, Hafthor, Hall, Wolverine, Hulk, Juggernaut, Kingpin, Abomination, Thor, Rex, Ollie). All match model.evaluate (max difference 6e-14). The check covers the Army official and Taylor equations (mean, range ±3.35), own body fat ± method error, the Kouri 12.5 ± 3 override, class ranges, height and weight ranges (Reeves, Coleman, Ramy, Shaw, Hafthor), comic editions kept apart, Wolverine at 88.5 kg, and the range rule (lowest mass and highest fat at the tallest height, and the reverse).

Wolverine scores 35.8 without adamantium and 55.0 with it (x1.54), so 'about one and a half times' is right. Rex's tail is 0.2894 m³ x 1,060 = 307 kg; the working tree now says 306, also fine. Ollie's tail is 11 kg. Rex scores 160 (126-189) and Ollie 182 (144-216) at skull heights 2.92 and 2.91 m. Rex's 426 px x 6.859 mm = 2.92 m.

Gaps: 41.83-62.50 (Kingpin to Darkseid), 87.73-125.76 (Abomination to Rex), 216.21-924.10 (Ollie to the end). No comparable build's range reaches into a gap. Edge cases behave: a wide range closes a gap, overstated or not-comparable builds do not fill one, a ratio of exactly 1.25 is not a gap, no top gap when top <= last high, and gaps cannot overlap (proved from the max-high / min-low construction). The only failure is that model.gaps throws on a list with no comparable builds, which real data never produces.

SEQ: bands and gaps are contiguous (12-25, 25-32, 32-41.83, gap, 62.50-87.73, gap, 125.76-216.21, gap, 924). HUMAN_TOP is 41.50 (Big Ramy's high) and the real-men-end rule sits after the 'top' band. Tags and rounding are consistent. gapStep picks Brian Shaw for gap 1 (ratio 1.50 against 1.494) and Sergio Oliva for gap 2. '924 is more than four times Ollie's top' is right (4.27). 'Roughly twice the top comic giants' is right (160/84 = 1.91).

Meatball 1.8 x 1,060 x π/6 x 0.925 = 924.1 (899.1 at 10% fat, 949.1 at 5%). A cylinder as wide as it is tall scores 1,386 ('about 1,400'); a cube scores 1,765 ('about 1,800'). The page rightly calls 924 a chosen end point, not a geometric maximum.

Limit definitions against code:
- Arms: armRestAngle tests below chest height, from 35% down the upper arm, against the torso, hip and thigh outline, at 30°.
- Thighs: thighContact binds at the lower-thigh station with vertical legs on axes at the hip joints (0.090 m = 0.05H, from Hara's 0.174 m spacing). The median soldier's gap there is 4.6 cm in the model ('about 4 cm', fact 4.4 cm); f=1.346 against the fact's 1.34.
- Face: elbowFlexion's surface-contact geometry is correct, and the crease is calibrated to 145° on the median soldier.
- 1.786 = (tan 40°/tan 17.5°)^(1/1.69).
- The order arms < thighs < face holds for every template.

Drawn volumes against weights (outline at 35°, measured by the tool): Banner +3%, p5 -4%, p50 +2%, p95 +7%, Kouri +10%, Reeves +11%, Coleman +20%, Big Ramy +20%, Wolverine +19%, Hall about 0%, Thor +9%, Hulk +2%, Abomination about 0% (Siri density). At a flat 1,060 kg/m³ the spread is -3% to +17%. The drawer's 'Drawing check' line gives exactly these figures (checked in 13 drawers on the rebuilt HEAD page).

Measuring tool on a smooth synthetic figure (elliptic-section torso with varying width and depth, ellipsoid head, conical legs, cylindrical arms at 30° and 40°):
- volume within -0.25% at 2,000 px, -0.6% at 800 px, and the same at H = 3 m
- chest, waist, thigh, calf, arm and forearm girths within 0.4% at 2,000 px (1.5% at 800 px)
- arm angle read as 30.00°
The arm slice formula π/4 · w² · armK · cos θ is exact for tilted cylinders.

Height checks: the tool rejects sheets whose views differ by 3% in every variant I tried (side stretched +3%, side scaled 1.03 uniformly, side -3%, back +3%, side +2.5%) and accepts +1.5%. Skull rows given for all views handle horns. The UI copies a single typed skull row to all views.
duo.jpg validation: frontOnly gives 2.545 m³ (2.54 on the page), inside the old methods' 2.52-2.60 m³. Parts are within 5% of the old checker, and the result holds across mask-threshold variations.
test/test.js (23/23), test/duo.js and test/shots.js all pass on a git-archive snapshot of HEAD 3cd65f5, rebuilt in scratchpad/review1/snap.
